• **Red algae:-**

• They are found in both** tropical and temperate waters** and play an important role in marine ecosystems as **primary producers and as a food source **for herbivorous marine animals.

• They are commonly found in** temperate and tropical regions** and play an important role in soil formation and nutrient cycling.
 
 
 
• **Phaeophyceae:**

questions.question: What will be the atomic number of an element X which is placed in period 2 and group 17?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**9.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Element X:-**

 
 
• The element X placed in period 2 and group 17 is a** halogen.**
 
• Halogens are **highly reactive non-metals **and have** 7 valence electrons **in their **outermost shell.**
 
• Since the element X is placed in group 17, it means it has** 7 valence electrons.**
 
• The **atomic number **of an element is equal to the** number of protons** in its nucleus.
 
• Therefore, the atomic number of element X will be 9 as it has** 9 protons in its nucleus.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://images-na.ssl-images-amazon.com/images/I/618HqUd9n6L.jpg] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The atomic number of **oxygen is 8**, which is the element placed in **period 2 and group 16.** 
 
• **Nitrogen** is the element placed in** period 2 and group 15** with an atomic number of **7. **
 
• The element with atomic number **10 is neon, **which is placed in** period 2** and group** 18.**

questions.question: Fisher’s quantity theory is explained by his famous equation given as ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**MV = PT.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fisher's quantity theory:-**

 
 
• It​ is a monetary theory that explains the relationship between** money supply, velocity of money, price level, and output**.
 
• The famous equation given by Fisher is **MV = PT, **where M is the money supply, V is the velocity of money, P is the price level, and T is the level of transactions.
 
• The equation suggests that an** increase in the money supply **(M) will lead to an **increase** in the price level (P), assuming that the velocity of money (V) and the level of transactions (T) are** constant.**
 
• The theory also implies that changes in the** money supply** have a direct impact on inflation, as an increase in the money supply leads to an **increase in the price level**, which in turn reduces the purchasing power of money.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The quantity theory of money has been subject to** criticism** over the years, with some economists arguing that it **oversimplifies the complex dynamics** of the economy.
 
• One of the criticisms is that the **velocity of money** is **not constant **and can vary significantly over time, making it difficult to predict the** impact of changes in the money supply **on the price level.
 
• Another criticism is that the theory assumes that the** level of transactions is fixed**, which is not always the case as it can be influenced by a variety of factors such as technology, demographics, and government policies.

• The textile industry was the **backbone of the Indian economy **during the pre-industrialization period.

• It was only after the British introduced the **electric power system **in India that the manufacturing of electricals began.
 
 
 
• **Chemicals:**
 
 
• Chemicals were **not** a major export from India during the pre-industrialization period.
 
• It was only after the** establishment of the chemical industry** in India that it became a major export.

• Light machinery was **not** manufactured in India during the pre-industrialization period.

questions.question: Who holds the authority of transferring judges from one High court to another High Court?

options.text: The senior most judge of Supreme Court

__
 
• President of India:-

 
 
• The** President of India** holds the authority of** transferring judges **from one High Court to another High Court.
 
• The president is elected by an electoral college consisting of the elected members of both houses of parliament and the elected members of the legislative assemblies of the states and union territories.
 
• The president serves a five-year term and can be re-elected .

• The **Chief Justice of India **is responsible for the **administration** of the Supreme Court and the High Courts.
 
• The **Law Minister of India **is responsible for the formulation and** implementation of laws and policies** related to the legal system of India.

questions.question: ___________ is the process of complete or incomplete oxidation or hydrolysis of fats and oils when exposed to air, light, moisture, or bacterial action that spoils food.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rancidification.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rancidification:-**

 
 
• It is a process of **spoilage of fats and oils** when exposed to** air, light, moisture, or bacterial action**.
 
• The oxidation process breaks down the** fatty acids** and produces **unpleasant odors and flavors** in the food.
 
• Rancidification can be prevented by storing food in **airtight containers, refrigeration, or adding antioxidants**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hydrogenation:-**

 
 
• It is a process of **adding hydrogen to unsaturated fats** to make them solid at room temperature, which is used to make margarine and shortening.
 
 
 
• **Auto-oxidation:-**
 
 
• It is a chemical reaction that occurs when** oxygen reacts with unsaturated fatty acids**, leading to the formation of free radicals and lipid peroxides.
 
 
 
• **Auto-reduction:-**
 
 
• It is a process of reducing a** chemical compound without the addition of external agents,** which is not related to the spoilage of food.

questions.question: Select the FALSE statement from the given options.

options.text: Baikal rocks are formed from the dissolved materials that precipitate from the solution.
The sedimentary rocks are formed by the deposition and subsequent cementation of that material within bodies of water and at the surface of the earth.
Metamorphic rocks may be formed simply by being deep beneath the Earth’s surface, subjected to high temperatures and the great pressure of the rock layers above it.
Igneous rock is formed through the cooling and solidification of magma or lava.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Baikal rocks are formed from the dissolved materials that precipitate from the solution.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Baikal rocks** are actually formed from the **solidification of magma or lava,** not from dissolved materials that precipitate from the solution. -
 
• **Sedimentary rocks** are indeed formed by the **deposition and subsequent cementation** of material within **bodies of water **and at the **surface of the earth.**
 
• **Metamorphic rocks **are formed by the** alteration of existing rock types** through** heat, pressure, or chemically active fluids.**
 
• **Igneous rocks **are indeed formed through the** cooling and solidification of magma or lava**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Baikal rocks **refer to the rocks found in the **Baikal Rift Zone, **a region of active tectonic activity in** Russia.**
 
• **Sedimentary rocks **are the most common type of rock on Earth and include types such as **sandstone, limestone, and shale.**
 
• **Metamorphic rocks **include types such as marble, slate, and gneiss and can be formed from sedimentary, igneous, or even other metamorphic rocks.
 
• **Igneous rocks** can be **intrusive **(formed from magma that cools slowly beneath the Earth's surface) or **extrusive** (formed from lava that cools quickly on the Earth's surface).

questions.question: Pathans in North-West India organised the society of Khudai Khidmatgars, popularly known as Red Shirt, under whose leadership?

• The movement was aimed at **promoting social reforms **and **political freedom **through peaceful means.
 
• The members of the movement wore** red shirts** as a symbol of their** unity and commitment to the cause.**
 
• Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan was a **Pashtun nationalist, a devout Muslim,** and a **close associate **of Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• He was also known as the **"Frontier Gandhi"** for his commitment to **non-violence** and his work towards **Hindu-Muslim unity.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Hasrat Mohan:-**

questions.question: Which of the following was established in Bombay in 1875?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Arya Samaj.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Arya Samaj:-**

 
 
• It was established in **Bombay.**
 
• Arya Samaj is a** Hindu reform movement** founded by **Swami Dayanand Saraswati** in **1875.**
 
• It aims to promote the Vedas as the only source of truth and to reject all forms of **idol worship, caste system, and superstitions.**
 
• The Arya Samaj played a significant role in the** Indian independence movement **and social reform movements such as the **abolition of child marriage and dowry system.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Satyashodhak Samaj:**

 
 
• It was founded by **Jyotirao Phule in 1873** in **Maharashtra.**
 
• It aimed to **fight against caste discrimination** and to provide **education to the lower castes. **
 
 
 
• **Aligarh movement:**
 
 
• It was founded by **Sir Syed Ahmed Khan in 1875 **in** Aligarh, Uttar Pradesh.**
 
• It aimed to promote** modern education** among Muslims and to create a** class of educated Muslims** who could work with the British government.
 
 
 
• **Brahmo Samaj:**
 
 
• It was founded by **Raja Ram Mohan Roy** in **1828 i**n **Kolkata.**
 
• It aimed to promote monotheism and to **reject idol worship, caste system, and other superstitions.**

questions.question: Which of the following options conveys the meaning of the word ‘Republic’ in the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Elected head.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Elected head:-**

 
 
• It conveys the meaning of the word** "Republic"** in the **Indian Constitution.**
 
• A republic is a form of government in which the head of state is elected by the** citizens or their representatives.**
 
• In India, the** President** is the head of state and is elected by an** electoral college** consisting of members of both houses of **Parliament and state legislatures.**
 
• The President holds a largely **ceremonial role **and acts as a **symbol of national unity**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nominated head:-**

 
 
• It​ refers to a **monarch or a person** appointed by a monarch.
 
 
 
• **Subordinate head:-**
 
 
• It​** **refers to a position **lower in rank **than the head.
 
 
 
• **Hereditary head:-**
 
 
• It​** **refers to a monarch or a person who** inherits the position of head of state. **
 
 

a1:T

questions.question: Who among the following was defeated in the battle of Chanderi in 1528?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Medini Rai.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Battle of Chanderi:-**

 
 
• It was fought on January 20, 1528, between the Mughal forces of Babur and the Rajput forces of Medini Rai, the ruler of Malwa.
 
• The battle took place in the aftermath of the Battle of Khanwa, in which Babur had defeated a Rajput confederacy led by Rana Sanga.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Babur** was the founder of the **Mughal Empire in India **and ruled from **1526 to 1530.**
 
• **Shershah Suri** was a ruler of the **Sur dynasty** who **defeated Humayun,** the son of Babur, and established the **Sur Empire** in India.
 
• **Sikandar Lodi ** was the most important ruler of the Lodi Dynasty, a part of India's Delhi Sultanate.
 
• He ascended Bahlul Lodi and was the dynasty's second ruler.
 
• In 1504 CE, he founded Agra city and made it his new Capital (earlier Delhi).
 
• **Ibrahim Lodi**** **was a ruler of the **Lodi dynasty **who ruled **Delhi before Babur's invasion.**
